title: Quarterly friction map for Dedicated Autoscale and initiative slices
creator: Ami Gupta
description:
Purpose:
Define a compact, cycle-aligned quarterly plan that surfaces operational friction points for Dedicated Autoscale, decomposes the initiative into 3 prioritized slices, and ties each slice to measurable OKRs. This ticket captures the product-level roadmap anchor, success metrics, rollout constraints, and the coordination plan with infra/eng and SRE.
milestones: M1 - Jan 20 to Feb 14: Friction discovery, stakeholder interviews, cost/latency telemetry baseline
M2 - Feb 15 to Mar 07: Scope discrete initiative slices + build acceptance criteria
M3 - Mar 08 to Mar 31: Pilot canaries for slice A (reservation hedging) and monitoring dashboards; finalize launch checklist
initiative_slices: Slice A - Reservation Hedging: short-term capacity hedging (pool smoothing + fast-fail autoscale) to reduce tail latency and missed SLOs
Slice B - Predictive Downsizing: conservative autoscale-down heuristics + billing signal hooks to reduce committed hours without affecting latency SLA
Slice C - Operator UX + Guardrails: console controls for pool slabs, burst budgets, and cost alerts for customers and support teams
success_metrics: Reduce SLO breach incidence for Dedicated pools during peak by 40% (baseline: Jan telemetry)
Decrease average committed GPU-hours per active customer pool by 12% for targeted test accounts
Time-to-fallback for capacity deficits (fallback model switch) < 250ms in 95th percentile
Customer-reported incidents related to autoscale <= 2 for pilot cohort
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry: dashboards show pre/post comparison for latency, cost per token, and reserved utilization
Canary: Slice A pilot on 3 dedicated pools for 2 weeks without >1 critical incident
Automation: autoscale policy config can be applied/rolled back from Console within 15 minutes
Docs: internal runbook + customer-facing KB drafted and reviewed by Support
risks: Underestimated cold-start latency when hedging reservations leading to increased 95th latency
Billing reconciliation edge-cases for split-hour committed reservations
Dependency on kernel scheduling change (ENG-45827) — if delayed, Slice A pilot scope must be reduced
Operator confusion if console labels/controls are inconsistent with existing pool settings
open_decisions: Decision 1: Narrow initial pilot to customers with predictable seq-lengths or include a broader variety? (input requested from Sales and Solutions)
Decision 2: Accept trade-off of slightly higher cost in exchange for lower tail latency for enterprise tiers? (PM + Finance)
roles_and_stakeholders: Product: Marisol Chen (owner), Ami Gupta (strategy lead)
Engineering: Rahul Kapoor (autoscale runtime), ENG-45827 owner
implementation_notes: Instrument KV cache hit-rate by reservation slab to detect ineffective hedging
Add a lightweight billing tag on hedged capacity for reconciliation in billing pipeline
Prototype autoscale policy template in staging and expose UI toggle in Console for pilot customers
Create an eval prompt set to track quality regressions caused by model fallbacks during autoscale events
updates: 2026-01-22 — Kickoff: stakeholder interview schedule completed (SRE, Eng, Support, Finance). Collected initial postmortem from 3 recent incidents to build friction hypotheses.
2026-01-28 — Telemetry baseline: first-pass dashboard shows dedicated pool utilization variance up to 38% across customers; capturing token-per-second distribution for pilot cohort.
2026-02-02 — Engineering spike (ENG-45827) landed a prototype for hedging allocator; needs perf regression test before can be used in pilot.
2026-02-10 — Decided to scope Slice A pilot to 3 medium-enterprise pools with seq-length homogeneity to reduce variance; asked Finance for temporary approval on hedged spend increase.
2026-02-14 — Draft runbook created and shared with SRE for review. Next: finalize canary schedule and create customer opt-in emails with Support.
